derivation_notes: The parent shared one hypoxic recruitment function between direct peripheral drive and hypoxic potentiation of the CO2 branch. Here only the potentiation pathway receives an additional oxygen-threshold offset, representing distinct peripheral transduction thresholds while preserving the same static clamp inputs and downstream motor saturation.
change_summary: The oxygen threshold for hypoxia-induced amplification of CO2 responsiveness is separated from the threshold for direct hypoxic drive by introducing Delta_P_O2_half_potentiation. This creates two CO2-dependent hypoxic threshold surfaces and changes the observable V_E(P_CO2,P_O2) mapping in the hypoxic transition region.

assumption_audit.released_assumption: A single shared hypoxic threshold surface in (P_O2,P_CO2) space governs all peripheral-hypoxia effects on ventilation.
assumption_audit.mechanism: Distinct peripheral transduction pathways can make hypoxia start to potentiate hypercapnic responsiveness at a different oxygen level than the level producing substantial direct hypoxic drive, even under steady arterial gas clamps.
assumption_audit.parent_reduction: The successor reduces to the parent when Delta_P_O2_half_potentiation = 0, making the potentiation threshold identical to the direct hypoxic-drive threshold.

response_change.parent_relation: The parent uses one shared CO2-dependent oxygen half-activation shift for both peripheral hypoxic drive and hypoxia-induced potentiation of CO2 responsiveness, so varying P_CO2 only translates both hypoxic effects together along the same P_O2 threshold axis.
response_change.child_relation: Allow the oxygen threshold governing hypoxia-induced potentiation of CO2 responsiveness to differ from the oxygen threshold governing direct peripheral hypoxic drive, creating two distinct CO2-dependent hypoxic recruitment surfaces within the same static clamp experiment.
response_change.observable_effect: At matched P_CO2, ventilation can begin to show amplified CO2 sensitivity at milder hypoxia while the direct hypoxic ventilatory increment remains small, or conversely require deeper hypoxia before CO2 potentiation appears; this changes the shape of V_E versus P_O2 across several fixed P_CO2 levels.

evolution_contract.observable_signature: When P_O2 is swept at several fixed P_CO2 clamps, the child can show one oxygen onset for the direct hypoxic rise in ventilation and a distinct oxygen onset for strengthened CO2 slope, so matched-P_CO2 slices can separate baseline hypoxic recruitment from hypoxic CO2 potentiation. The parent cannot produce that separation because both effects share the same translated hypoxic threshold function.
evolution_contract.shortcut_blocked: A single parent parameter set cannot generally absorb this change because any refit that moves the shared hypoxic threshold to match the oxygen onset of direct hypoxic drive necessarily moves the oxygen onset of CO2 potentiation by the same amount, and vice versa. Across the same collection of fixed-P_CO2 slices, the child permits two distinct onset locations in P_O2 while the parent is structurally constrained to one shared onset surface.

evolution_plan.gap_statement: The current model assumes that the same oxygen recruitment curve controls both direct peripheral hypoxic drive and hypoxia-dependent amplification of CO2 sensitivity, which is a restrictive idealization of carotid-body transduction.
evolution_plan.baseline_assumption: A single shared hypoxic threshold surface in (P_O2,P_CO2) space governs all peripheral-hypoxia effects on ventilation.
evolution_plan.scientific_mechanism: Distinct peripheral transduction pathways can make hypoxia start to potentiate hypercapnic responsiveness at a different oxygen level than the level producing substantial direct hypoxic drive, even under steady arterial gas clamps.
evolution_plan.rationale: Vary P_O2 while holding P_CO2 fixed, then compare several fixed P_CO2 slices. In the parent, once all parameters are globally refit, the onset of direct hypoxic ventilation and the onset of hypoxic amplification of the CO2 branch must remain locked because both are driven by the same H_parent(P_O2,P_CO2). A child with separate hypoxic thresholds for these two pathways can produce a concrete contrast: at moderate hypoxia, V_E may show little direct hypoxic rise yet already exhibit stronger dependence on P_CO2, or the reverse. This is an observable change in the scored static mapping V_E(P_CO2,P_O2), not merely an auxiliary reinterpretation. The contrast is admissible in the sampled steady-clamp setting, especially when motor saturation is incomplete and P_O2 lies near the hypoxic transition range set by S_O2. A single parent parameter set cannot generally reproduce two different hypoxic onset locations for these two effects across the same collection of P_CO2 clamps, because moving the shared threshold to fit one branch necessarily moves the other with it.

selected_embedding_pattern.description: Use a finite-capacity, saturation, threshold, or regime-transition response.

scenario_text: Arterial carbon dioxide and oxygen tensions are independently clamped while steady minute ventilation is measured in a resting subject. The target is the integrated ventilatory output of central and peripheral chemoreceptor drive under fixed metabolic demand. Ventilation rises with carbon dioxide and is amplified when oxygen tension becomes low, but respiratory motor output has a finite physiological ceiling. Acid-base adaptation and temporal response delays are excluded from the baseline experiment.
